decisions.executionNote: Approach the right-side gray nut with the right arm, gradually adopting an elbow-up downward grasp orientation. Height and final centering will be checked visually.
Complete the right gray-nut approach with small continuous elbow-up increments, then descend toward the nut without closing until visually centered.
Lower the remaining few millimeters, close on the gray nut, and lift vertically to check retention in RGB before moving to its matching screw.
Gray nut is visibly retained. Carry it left within the right workspace over the gray screw, then lower to the initial insertion height; verify alignment before tightening.
Refine gray nut centering by a few millimeters, lower to screw-tip engagement, then begin a small clockwise tightening stroke while retaining the nut.
Continue the gray clockwise stroke with a small axial feed, release for re-indexing, and rotate the open gripper back without intentionally reversing the nut.
Gray nut remains upright around the screw tip. Finish open re-indexing, regrasp, then apply the next clockwise tightening stroke with minimal axial feed.
Continue clockwise gray-nut tightening while holding closed, then open and partially re-index. The screw remains centered in the nut in the wrist view.
Re-index the open right gripper, close on the gray nut again, and continue clockwise tightening in small increments.
Complete this gray-nut clockwise stroke with a gentle downward feed, then release and begin open re-indexing. Maintain the current upright alignment.
Re-index without holding the gray nut, then close and start another clockwise stroke. The nut remains upright and the screw cap is visible inside its bore.
Finish the gray clockwise stroke, release the nut, and lift clear to inspect the assembled pair before selecting the next color.
Gray pair remains upright after release. Move the right gripper above the red nut and descend cautiously; it will be staged centrally for the left arm rather than crossing arms.
Descend onto the centered red nut, close, and lift vertically. Check the wrist and head views for retention before transferring to the central staging area.
The red nut is visibly retained. Carry it to the central staging area on the right side of the midline and lower to table height for a sequential handover.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no preceding motion occurred. Release and clear the staged red nut with the right arm while the left starts a gradual elbow-up approach on its own side.
The red nut is resting at the central staging spot. Clear the right arm farther right and bring the left arm above the staging area with a continuous elbow-up, downward-facing approach.
Lower the left gripper onto the staged red nut at the midline, keeping the right arm clear. Check centering before closing.
Refine left-gripper centering on the staged red nut, close, and lift vertically to verify a secure handover from the table.
The red nut is retained by the left gripper. Carry it above the red screw for alignment; independently position the open right gripper above the yellow nut, maintaining arm separation.
Lower and refine the red nut onto its screw, beginning a gentle clockwise turn. On the right, descend to the yellow nut and close without yet transporting it.
Pause red rotation to improve screw-tip alignment by a few millimeters and lower gently. Lift the yellow nut and carry it to the central staging area, keeping the arms separated.
Lower the red nut gently with a short clockwise stroke, then release and begin re-indexing to inspect seating. Set the yellow nut down centrally and open before lifting the right gripper clear.
Red nut is visibly separate after release, so it needs regrasping and improved alignment. Lift and approach its new table location; move the right arm clear of the staged yellow nut.
Regrasp the red nut at its new table location and lift slightly. Keep the right arm stationary and clear while verifying retention.
Red nut is retained. Lift for clearance and align above the red screw using the current head geometry, pausing above contact to inspect the screw tip rather than forcing insertion.
Correct the small lateral red-nut offset seen in the wrist view and descend slowly to screw-tip height, holding orientation fixed to check engagement before turning.
The red screw tip is now visible inside the nut bore. Apply a controlled clockwise stroke with minimal downward feed, then open to check that the nut stays seated.
The red nut tilted after release, so seating is not established. Re-index the open gripper, gently regrasp, and lift slightly to inspect its orientation before another alignment attempt.
The red nut is now resting separately on the table, not retained. Re-approach its observed location with an open left gripper; use the exposed screw base to improve the next alignment.
Center and close on the red nut again, then lift it clear for another carefully aligned insertion attempt. The yellow nut remains staged and the right arm stays clear.
Bring the retained red nut above the screw axis with clearance and hold for a fresh alignment check; avoid turning while lateral seating remains uncertain.
The red screw stem is nearly centered behind the nut. Make a millimeter-scale lateral correction and descend without rotation, then inspect the bore for actual tip engagement.
The red screw cap is centered within the nut bore. Apply a slow clockwise stroke without additional downward feed and keep the nut held for a visual seating check before releasing.
The red screw now visibly enters the nut deeply. Open and re-index the left gripper without translating, checking whether the nut remains upright on the screw.
Red nut remains upright and engaged after opening. Lower slightly to regrasp its sides and apply another slow clockwise tightening stroke without pushing downward during rotation.
Red nut remains aligned with the screw cap well inside its bore. Open, re-index without translating, and regrasp for another tightening stroke.
Apply another controlled clockwise red-nut stroke with very slight axial feed, then open to verify that it remains seated and upright.
Red nut stays upright after release. Re-index the open gripper and close again for another clockwise tightening stroke without disturbing its axis.
Continue red clockwise tightening with a minimal feed, then release while keeping the gripper stationary to inspect the assembled pair.
Red nut remains upright and deeply seated after release. Lift clear and bring the open left gripper above the centrally staged yellow nut while keeping the right arm separated.
Center the open left gripper over the staged yellow nut and descend gradually to grasp height, keeping the right arm clear and stationary.
Make a small wrist-view centering correction on the yellow nut, close, and lift vertically to verify retention before moving into the left workspace.
Yellow nut is visibly retained. Lift for clearance and carry it toward the yellow screw in the left workspace, staying above the completed red pair.
Align the held yellow nut over the visible yellow screw tip, staying above contact for a wrist-view check before insertion.
Correct the yellow screw's leftward offset in the wrist view, then lower the nut slowly without rotation to inspect tip engagement.
Yellow tip is still visibly offset from the bore. Hold height and adjust laterally using the observed wrist response, then inspect before any tightening.
Yellow screw and nut are nearly centered laterally. Make a small correction and lower slowly without turning, inspecting for the screw cap inside the bore.
The yellow screw cap is centered within the nut bore. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke without additional descent, then open to verify upright seating.
Yellow nut stays upright after release. Re-index the open left gripper and close again for the next clockwise tightening stroke, preserving the current alignment.
Continue clockwise tightening of the seated yellow nut with minimal axial feed, then release and inspect its stability.
Yellow nut remains upright with its screw cap visible. Re-index the open gripper and regrasp without translating for another clockwise tightening stroke.
Apply the next clockwise yellow-nut tightening stroke, then release to check that the assembly remains upright and seated.
Re-index the open left gripper around the stable yellow assembly, then regrasp for one more controlled tightening stroke.
Finish the yellow clockwise tightening stroke and open the gripper, preserving the upright assembly before retracting.
Yellow remains upright after release. Lift both open grippers clear of the three assemblies and re-index the left wrist toward a continuous elbow-up return posture.
All three pairs remain together after release. Begin a gradual, separated-arm return toward the original poses with grippers open and elbows kept in the continuous upper configuration.
Complete the separated, elbow-up return toward both original EE poses, keeping both grippers open and leaving the assembled pairs undisturbed.
Settle both open grippers at the original poses and inspect the three upright color-matched assemblies without disturbing them.
The gray screw cap appears more recessed than the other two. Re-approach it with the right arm for a closer seating check and possible further tightening; leave the left arm at origin.
Complete the gradual right-arm approach above the gray pair, keeping the gripper open and clear of contact for an updated seating view.
Lower to the gray nut's sides while re-indexing the open right gripper, then close for additional tightening. Preserve the upright nut-screw alignment.
Apply a slow clockwise gray-nut stroke without pushing down, then open and inspect whether the screw cap advances within the bore.
Gray nut remains upright but its cap is recessed. Re-index the open right gripper and regrasp for a controlled stroke with a small axial advance.
Advance the gray nut with a slow clockwise stroke and a small controlled downward feed, then release to inspect depth and upright seating.
Re-index and regrasp the gray nut, then make a small lateral centering adjustment toward the screw axis; inspect before further downward motion.
Apply another slow clockwise gray-nut stroke with only a millimeter of axial feed, then release to inspect the seating without forcing it.
Re-index the open right gripper with a small tilt correction and regrasp the gray nut; depth remains uncertain, so preserve its lateral alignment.
Turn the gray nut clockwise with a gradual six-millimeter axial advance, then release to inspect whether it seats deeper while remaining upright.
Gray depth is not visibly improving. Clear and regrasp its upper sides at a different jaw angle, then make a small lift to check retention and alignment rather than continuing to push.
The gray assembly remains together during the small lift check. Release and withdraw the right gripper, leaving all three pairs undisturbed and beginning a gradual return to origin.
Continue the open right-arm return along a continuous elbow-up path. Make a tiny correction to the left origin pose while leaving all three upright assemblies untouched.
Finish returning the right arm to its original pose with the gripper open and settle both arms, leaving the three assembled pairs undisturbed.
Hold both open grippers at origin and allow the three upright matched assemblies to settle; gray thread depth remains less visually certain than red and yellow.
Maintain the original open-gripper poses with only tiny drift corrections; the matched assemblies remain upright and undisturbed.
Recheck the gray nut at its upper gripping height rather than the screw shaft; begin a gradual right-arm approach while leaving the other two pairs untouched.
